_meta.description: Shell plc financials. Revenue & net income are IFRS (net income = income attributable to Shell plc shareholders). Capex = cash capital expenditure. Production = total available for sale (kboe/d). Dividend = declared per ordinary share (USD). Cash flow = cash flow from operating activities (USD bn). Net debt = Shell-reported net debt (USD bn).
_meta.note: Company was 'Royal Dutch Shell plc' through 2021, 'Shell plc' from Jan 2022. 2020 = COVID loss year & the first dividend cut since WWII. 2022 = record profit. Net debt peaked after the 2016 BG Group acquisition.

metrics.label: Revenue
metrics.desc: Total money taken in from selling energy and products — the top line, before costs.

metrics.label: Net income
metrics.desc: Profit (or loss) for shareholders after all costs and taxes — the bottom line.

metrics.label: Operating cash flow
metrics.desc: Cash generated by day-to-day operations — a key gauge of financial health.

metrics.label: Capital expenditure
metrics.desc: Cash invested in building and maintaining assets like platforms, plants and projects.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.desc: Debt minus cash (Shell-reported). Peaked after the 2016 BG Group acquisition, then fell.
metrics.source: Shell Q4 results releases (gearing & net debt)

metrics.label: Dividend / share
metrics.desc: Declared dividend per ordinary share. Note the ~66% cut in 2020, then a steady rebuild.
metrics.source: stockanalysis.com / dividendmax (per ordinary share; NYSE ADR ≈ 2×)

metrics.label: Oil & gas production
metrics.desc: Oil and gas produced per day, in thousands of barrels of oil equivalent.
metrics.source: Shell annual reports (total available for sale)

segmentEarnings._meta: Adjusted Earnings by segment (USD bn). Renewables & Energy Solutions and Corporate were negative in 2024. Confidence: verified.

sharePrice._meta: Indexed growth comparison on ONE consistent basis: NOMINAL year-end closing PRICE (price-only, excludes dividends) for all series. This keeps the comparison fair — no mixing of dividend-adjusted and nominal data. Values are APPROXIMATE periodic year-end closes, NOT a precise market feed. The chart rebases each selected series to 100 at the start of the chosen range, so it shows percentage price growth, not absolute price. Not investment advice. (A total-return view including reinvested dividends would lift the dividend-paying companies and the S&P 500 somewhat; gold pays none.)

series.label: S&P 500
series.source: S&P 500 year-end index closes — price index (multpl.com)

series.label: Gold
series.source: Gold year-end close, USD/oz (JM Bullion / bullion-rates)

callouts.label: COVID demand collapse — net loss of $21.7B & a ~66% dividend cut
